interpretation: Source/CI test success is not full contract acceptance. This is an evidence-gap inventory that mirrors the owner ledger, not a change to it. Each case was re-reviewed on 2026-10-14 against docs/v5/progress.json as reconciled in docs/v5.1/release/ACCEPTANCE-CASE-RECONCILIATION-20261014.md: LEDGER_PASS entries record statuses the owner ledger already accepted, RUNNING entries name the remaining reachable work, and BLOCKED entries name the exact external gate. No source or CI result promotes a case by itself.

evidence_baseline.disclaimer: Real disposable-service CI and native source builds, not proof of production staging, signed physical devices, providers or cutover.

cases.title: Product/source freeze
cases.remaining_proof: Android device and desktop four-theme captures exist (phase00-visual-baseline), but the iOS physical-device theme matrix and the final native/browser exception register remain outstanding; primary release-doc proof sits in docs/v5.1/release/DEVICE-ANDROID-EB2101-20261014.md and NATIVE-BUILDS-20261013.md.

cases.title: Baseline and CI
cases.remaining_proof: Baseline ancestry and the V4 protected tags are verified, but the exact-head all-green 12-workflow Actions run ID for the frozen candidate is still unrecorded; record it and re-sign A02 (adjacent proof in docs/v5.1/release/STAGE-D-RELEASE-QUALIFICATION-20261014.md).

cases.title: Reported backup conflict
cases.remaining_proof: Already PASS in the owner ledger: the E1 read-only V4 Restic inspection (611 snapshots, byte-identical off-box restore, quick_check ok) plus the V5-only R2 bucket and live host alerts; retain snapshot IDs, retrieval checksums and the restore log (release-doc proof: docs/v5.1/release/E1-V4-SNAPSHOT-RESTORE-20261014.md).

cases.title: Environment and role isolation
cases.remaining_proof: Already PASS in the owner ledger: distinct least-privilege api/core/worker/backup/audit roles verified with real production 42501 denials; retain the role probes and regression logs at the release SHA.

cases.title: Migration framework
cases.remaining_proof: Already PASS in the owner ledger: 49/49 checksummed migrations applied from zero with SCRAM channel binding and a verified idempotent re-run; retain migration checksums, create/upgrade logs and the lock test.

cases.title: Complete source coverage
cases.remaining_proof: Already PASS in the owner ledger: the production import coverage inventory recorded 35 tables, 14 indexes, 2 triggers, 8,549 rows and 44,197 fields with zero unclassified locators against the source fingerprint; retain the coverage manifest (release-doc proof: docs/v5.1/release/E2-PRODUCTION-IMPORT-RECONCILIATION-20261014.md).

cases.title: Per-actor reconciliation
cases.remaining_proof: Already PASS in the owner ledger: the production reconcile gate passed with unexplained:0 and all nine conservation equations holding over real actors; retain the sanitized difference summary and the swapped-wallet negative check.

cases.title: Deterministic restartable import
cases.remaining_proof: Deterministic single import and fixture-level interruption/resume are proven, but a repeated/interrupted replay and a quarterly boundary rollover on the frozen production snapshot remain unexecuted.

cases.title: Escrow and ledger
cases.remaining_proof: Already PASS in the owner ledger: per-asset escrow/ledger invariants C1-C6 pass with zero failures over real production data; retain the source-linked accounting baseline and transaction tests.

cases.title: Concurrent spending
cases.remaining_proof: Contention/atomicity and concurrent accepts are proven, but same-actor races across entry, challenge, conversion and tournament reservation with final wallet rows remain unexecuted against the deployed Core.

cases.title: Atomic result and payout
cases.remaining_proof: Already PASS in the owner ledger: a forced mid-transaction crash rolled back with zero wallet/ledger/outbox effects and the retry committed exactly once; retain the fault-injection log and before/after invariants.

cases.title: Shared actor identity
cases.remaining_proof: Blocked externally: Google and Apple OAuth are unconfigured and the Android prototype is offline-only, so a real cross-provider actor-hash comparison on signed mobile clients cannot be produced yet (primary proof: docs/v5.1/release/PROVIDER-READINESS-INVENTORY-20261013.md).

cases.title: Refresh and revocation
cases.remaining_proof: Live cookie/session revocation and presence fencing are proven, but physical-device refresh races, old-token replay and active socket key rotation under configured provider sessions remain unexecuted.

cases.title: One-use realtime tickets
cases.remaining_proof: Single-node realtime ticket subscribe and redemption are proven, but concurrent two-node redemption and replay after Redis loss remain unexecuted on the deployed topology (staging operates a single Core).

cases.title: Redis complete loss
cases.remaining_proof: Durable decisions survive complete ephemera loss on a disposable lab, but a real staging Redis (Upstash) wipe during an active match and paid queue remains unexecuted.

cases.title: Matcher concurrency
cases.remaining_proof: Already PASS in the owner ledger: concurrent matcher races produced at most one assignment with zero double-seated players and zero charges at offer; retain the load trace and the assignment constraint results.

cases.title: Committed move recovery
cases.remaining_proof: Already PASS in the owner ledger: a real-socket SIGKILL after a committed move was reconstructed by the second Core with retry deduplication; retain the operation/revision trace and the failover demonstration.

cases.title: Clock correctness
cases.remaining_proof: Already PASS in the owner ledger: durable clocks settle a due timeout once, commit exactly one effect under concurrent move/timeout, pay a replayed key once and survive Redis loss; retain the deterministic boundary tests.

cases.title: Transport recovery
cases.remaining_proof: HTTP snapshot fallback, reconnect delta and duplicate safety are proven on the deployed origin, but physical-device backgrounding, offline reconnect and notification reordering remain unrun on native devices.

cases.title: Tournament behavior
cases.remaining_proof: Host-leave cancellation, pause/resume and indivisible settlement pass in local and capture labs, but no multi-worker public/private tournament run exists on deployed staging (the API mounts no tournament route).

cases.title: Jobs and outbox
cases.remaining_proof: Durable lease fencing, outbox retry and claim crash recovery are proven on a disposable PG lab, but real provider I/O crash/retry/DLQ scenarios remain unexecuted on integrated staging.

cases.title: UTC scheduled economics
cases.remaining_proof: Already PASS in the owner ledger: seeded UTC scheduling tests show stable period identities, one effect under two concurrent schedulers and ordered downtime catch-up across the week boundary; retain the unique business-operation records.

cases.title: Vercel/Core ownership
cases.remaining_proof: Already PASS in the owner ledger: the public Core gateway returned the required 403/401/404s and the Vercel API holds only api_runtime with zero Core pool; retain the negative security tests and the sanitized distributed request trace.

cases.title: Retained browser compatibility
cases.remaining_proof: Blocked externally: old-origin browser E2E and session continuity require the authorised V5 facade cutover; until then the residual V4 SQLite writer stays live and the comparison cannot be run (primary proof: docs/v5.1/release/P3-EDGE-V4-REGRESSION-20261013.md).

cases.title: Cache correctness and privacy
cases.remaining_proof: Already PASS in the owner ledger: versioned projections reject stale sequence updates, private responses are no-cache, and exact 64-bit decimals plus an honest 503 were observed on the deployed signed Core; retain the cache replay and isolation report.

cases.title: Private operations and audit
cases.remaining_proof: Public edge blocks non-ingress paths and audit_runtime is restricted on production, but an external probe of the private staging ops/audit endpoints and a concurrent audit-chain verification remain unrecorded.

cases.title: Operational diagnosis and alerting
cases.remaining_proof: Incident and recovery alert delivery is proven on the V4 host, but V5 staging-specific signals (API/Core/Neon/backup/worker) still lack wired thresholds and no cross-service support-ID trace has been executed (adjacent proof: docs/v5.1/release/DELIVERED-ALERTS-20261014.md).

cases.title: Independent restore
cases.remaining_proof: Already PASS in the owner ledger on measured independent backup/restore evidence: a real production pg_dump was sealed, uploaded to a new V5-only R2 bucket, re-fetched under an independent credential with matching sha256 and restored into an isolated PG16 target with row-for-row equality; retain measured RPO/RTO and cleanup (release-doc proof: docs/v5.1/release/P15-V5-BACKUP-RETRIEVE-MEASURED-20261014.md).

cases.title: Process vs host availability
cases.remaining_proof: Core process redundancy and drain failover pass in the real-socket loopback lab, but a real Core kill during an active match plus a measured same-host outage RTO remain unrun on staging.

cases.title: Immutable release compatibility
cases.remaining_proof: Blocked externally: production V5 image digests and the cutover window are unavailable (E3 pending), so no component-skew deploy or application rollback can be executed against real release manifests (adjacent proof: docs/v5.1/release/STAGE-D-RELEASE-QUALIFICATION-20261014.md).

cases.title: Capacity and degradation
cases.remaining_proof: Tiered load and chaos are profiled only on a small synthetic disposable fixture (MEASURED_ADAPTER_ONLY_NOT_LAUNCH_CAPACITY); realistic-history load, dependency saturation and backpressure on the deployed topology remain unexecuted.

cases.title: Real native artifacts and offline bundle
cases.remaining_proof: Blocked externally: signed iOS artifacts require Apple Developer enrollment (0 signing identities), so only the prototype Android physical install, offline launch and bundle parity can be shown now (primary proof: docs/v5.1/release/DEVICE-IOS-IPHONE16PRO-20261014.md).

cases.title: Native bridge security
cases.remaining_proof: Native bridge and asset security contracts pass locally (30/30) and the Android APK drops INTERNET/AD_ID, but untrusted-frame injection and storage/backup extraction remain unexercised on physical devices.

cases.title: Native purchases and restore
cases.remaining_proof: Blocked externally: no registered store products, sandbox testers or provider credentials exist and store approval is pending, so real Crown purchase/restore flows cannot be exercised (primary proof: docs/v5.1/release/PROVIDER-READINESS-INVENTORY-20261013.md).

cases.title: Ads and consent
cases.remaining_proof: Blocked externally: the AdMob publisher account is unverified and UMP consent plus the iOS tracking declarations are unapproved, so real ad SSV/consent behaviour cannot be measured on device.

cases.title: Native accessibility and parity
cases.remaining_proof: Blocked externally: the iOS device matrix and VoiceOver verification require Apple Developer enrollment; only the physical Android themes and structural accessibility checks can be shown now.

cases.title: Distribution and review truthfulness
cases.remaining_proof: Blocked externally: there are no signing identities, provisioning profiles or store console records, so real submission/review states cannot be demonstrated and the release scripts fail closed by design.

cases.title: Single writer and first-write fence
cases.remaining_proof: Blocked externally: only an authorised cutover window can stop the V4 writers and transfer the authority epoch; mutation paths are inventoried and the import is verified, but no epoch was transferred and no first V5 write was logged.

cases.title: Rollback classes
cases.remaining_proof: Blocked externally: rehearsals beyond the quarantined P15 drills require the authorised cutover window, so release-topology pre-write abort and post-write recovery remain unproven.

cases.title: Retirement and scaling discipline
cases.remaining_proof: Blocked externally: retirement and the post-cutover scaling review require an executed G22; V4/SQLite remains the sole live authority, so no real post-cutover demand metrics exist.
